deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page, f.34): given one rational point (xi,ups) on the conic a x^2+2b xy+c y^2+2d x+2e y+f=0, Gauss gives the rational parametrization of all its points by a parameter z, with D=b^2-ac:
 x=(xi+2(b xi+c ups+e)z+(D xi+2be-2cd)z^2)/(1-Dz^2)
 y=(ups-2(a xi+b ups+d)z+(D ups+2bd-2ae)z^2)/(1-Dz^2).
This page inverts that map. Given two points (xi,ups) and (x,y) of the conic, it computes the parameter z that carries the first to the second.

(1) Change of letters (top left). The cancelled 'f=u' is followed by z=1/f, f=(t+1)/u, hence z=u/(t+1). This is the standard rational parametrization of the Pell-type conic t^2-Du^2=1 [my addition: t=(1+Dz^2)/(1-Dz^2), u=2z/(1-Dz^2), so t+1=2/(1-Dz^2)].

(2) Centred coordinates. Put g=be-cd and h=bd-ae (the margin products 'bde-cdd', 'bde-aee' are dg and eh). Then:
 m=Dx+g, n=Dy+h, M=D xi+g, N=D ups+h;
 equivalently x=(m+cd-be)/D, y=(n+ae-bd)/D, and similarly for xi, ups.
So m,n,M,N are D times coordinates relative to the centre of the conic.

(3) Automorph. The map is
 m = t M + u(bM+cN), n = t N - u(aM+bN),
i.e. the matrix [[t+bu, cu],[-au, t-bu]] of determinant t^2-Du^2. It multiplies the form aX^2+2bXY+cY^2 by t^2-Du^2, so it preserves the form when t^2-Du^2=1. This is the automorph of Disquisitiones art. 162, used here rationally. Substituting t and u in terms of z reproduces exactly the previous page's formulas (verified).

(4) Two identities, checked:
 bM+cN = D(b xi+c ups+e)
 aM+bN = D(a xi+b ups+d).

(5) Elimination of t. Add (M,N) to both sides:
 (t+1)M+u(bM+cN)=m+M
 (t+1)N-u(aM+bN)=n+N.
Cross-multiplying gives
 (t+1)(Mn-Nm) + u[aMm+b(Mn+Nm)+cNn+aMM+2bMN+cNN] = 0.
Hence
 z = u/(t+1) = (Nm-Mn)/[aMm+b(Mn+Nm)+cNn+aMM+2bMN+cNN].
The denominator equals (m+M)(aM+bN)+(n+N)(bM+cN) = D[(m+M)(a xi+b ups+d)+(n+N)(b xi+c ups+e)].

(6) Numerator. The top-right scratch expands Nm-Mn = D^2(ups x - y xi) + D(g ups - h xi + h x - g y). On the body of the page Gauss writes only 'Numerator = DD(x ups - y xi)' and concludes
 z = D(x ups - y xi)/[(m+M)(a xi+b ups+d)+(n+N)(b xi+c ups+e)].

(7) Expanding the denominator.
- M-part: M(a xi+b ups+d)+N(b xi+c ups+e) = D(a xi^2+2b xi ups+c ups^2+2d xi+2e ups) - (ae^2-2bde+cd^2). This is correct. On the conic it equals -(Df+ae^2-2bde+cd^2) = det[[a,b,d],[b,c,e],[d,e,f]] [my identification].
- m-part: written as D xi(ax+by+d) + D ups(bx+cy+e) + D(dx+ey). This equals the m-part apart from the constant dg+eh = 2bde-cd^2-ae^2 (an ink blot obscures part of this line).
- [My completion:] the bracket equals D·B + 2·Delta, where B = x(a xi+b ups+d)+y(b xi+c ups+e)+d xi+e ups+f is the polar bilinear form and Delta is the 3x3 determinant. So z = (Nm-Mn)/(D(D·B+2·Delta)).

Test case: x^2-y^2=1 with base point (1,0). The formula returns z correctly.
errors: The statement 'Numerator = DD(x ups - y xi)' drops terms. The correct value is Nm - Mn = D^2(x ups - y xi) + D[g(ups-y) + h(x-xi)], with g=be-cd and h=bd-ae. Gauss's own top-right scratch shows these extra terms. It also omits -Dyg.

Consequently the displayed z = D(x ups - y xi)/[(m+M)(a xi+b ups+d)+(n+N)(b xi+c ups+e)] is correct only when g(ups-y)+h(x-xi)=0, e.g. when d=e=0 (conic centred at the origin). The correct numerator is D(x ups - y xi)+g(ups-y)+h(x-xi).

The third line of the 'Denom.' expansion (D xi(ax+by+d)+D ups(bx+cy+e)+D(dx+ey)) omits the constant dg+eh = -(ae^2-2bde+cd^2) from the m-part. It may be absorbed in the blotted bracket, but this cannot be confirmed.

results.what: Inverse of the one-point rational parametrization of a conic: the parameter z expressed rationally in terms of the base point and the target point, via elimination from the automorph relations.
results.modern_name: Rational parametrization of a conic / birational map P^1 <-> conic and its inverse
results.usually_credited_to: Diophantus; Euler; Lagrange (rational points on conics)

results.what: Use of the automorph matrix [[t+bu, cu],[-au, t-bu]] with t^2-Du^2=1, rationally parametrized by z=u/(t+1), to move points on a central conic.
results.modern_name: Automorphs of binary quadratic forms (orthogonal group of the form), Cayley-type rational parametrization
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange; Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae art. 162 (integral case)

results.what: The identity M(a xi+b ups+d)+N(b xi+c ups+e) = -(Df+ae^2-2bde+cd^2) = 3x3 determinant on the conic, with D=b^2-ac.
results.modern_name: Discriminant of a ternary quadratic form / value of the form at the centre

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine algebraic scratch work inverting a conic parametrization built on Gauss's own automorph theory. The method is classical and is clearly Gauss's style. It contains a minor slip in the numerator.
